Subject: Promo credit ask for AWS catalog pilot

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood’s latency profile and the dedicated capacity option. We’re preparing a short pilot (3 months) to list an integration in AWS Marketplace and want to understand options for promotional listing credits for the initial go-to-market.

Specifics: BrightRetail will commit to a 3-month pilot with an estimated $28k of invoiceable usage across the catalog listing and co-sell activities. To make the economics work for our procurement, we’re asking if Redwood can provide a one-time catalog promotional credit of $10k applied to the marketplace billing or a marketplace-friendly private-offer credit.

Procurement asked that any exception be documented so they can process vendor onboarding (SOC docs already in progress). Please let me know what data you need from our side and an internal timeline for approvals.

Best,
Olivia

Thanks Hannah — quick read: Finance is ok with pilot credits but prefers structure vs one-off. Proposal: convert the $10k ask into either a) $8k marketplace-friendly private-offer credit plus $2k in go-to-market co-marketing funds, or b) scaled credit: 25% credit on first-month billed usage capped at $9k. Both require written approval from Marketplace Partnerships for any private-offer flow.

If BrightRetail is willing to sign a 3-month MRC commitment for dedicated capacity (even at a reduced profile) we can consider $10k total consideration across credits + marketing. Otherwise push for the scaled credit (option b).

Quick update on the marketplace side after a call with our AWS partner rep:
- AWS will accept a private-offer credit, but it must be requested via their partner portal and documented as a buyer-side credit tied to the private-offer. That means the credit shows on the AWS invoice as a marketplace rebate (buyer benefit) and AWS reconciles with us separately.
- Marketplace team is comfortable with $8k as buyer-side private-offer credit. Any additional $2k should be packaged as co-marketing funds (not on the invoice).
- Timeline: portal request + approvals = ~7 business days. DocuSign flow for private-offer required.

Recommendation: Offer option A from Ben: $8k private-offer credit + $2k co-marketing. Finance will need the funding source for the $2k (marketing budget vs sales MDF). Ben / Marcus — can you confirm which bucket covers the $2k?

Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Marketplaces
Redwood Inference

Olivia / BrightRetail team — thanks for your patience. Internal approvals are in and we can support your pilot with the following structure: 

1) $8,000 private-offer credit applied on the AWS Marketplace invoice (buyer benefit). Redwood will submit the private-offer credit request via the AWS partner portal; expected approval cycle ~7 business days.
2) $2,000 co-marketing credit to be used for joint PR/launch and co-branded collateral. This will be processed as marketing funds — BrightRetail should provide W-9 and standard co-marketing SOW (one-page).
3) Private-offer DocuSign and pilot MOU to be executed before listing.

Next steps: Hannah — can you coordinate DocuSign and confirm whether BrightRetail will sign the 3-month pilot MOU for dedicated capacity? Olivia — if you can confirm funding cadence and send W-9, procurement can kick off onboarding.

Thanks — looking forward to the launch.
